summary.headline: Ardee Q2 FY27 revenue rose 33.5% YoY to Rs. 325 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 8.9% on costlier imported raw material and fuel.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue was Rs. 325 crore (up 33.5% YoY from Rs. 243 crore), with EBITDA of Rs. 29 crore (8.9% margin) and PAT of Rs. 18 crore on sales volume of 15,656 MT. H1 FY27 revenue was Rs. 664 crore (up 34%), EBITDA Rs. 63 crore and PAT Rs. 38 crore on 33,300 MT volume. Management attributed margin compression to higher imported raw material and freight costs linked to the war and Hormuz disruption, plus higher fuel and opex, with expensive procurement lagging into the P&L by two to three months. Management shifted its focus to absolute growth and volume, maintained the 10-15% FY27 volume growth target, and guided that per-ton margins would stay around current levels.

segments.name: Domestic lead recycling
segments.commentary: Domestic battery scrap share of procurement reportedly rose to about 27-28% from about 15% a year earlier, sourced via auctions from tower companies and corporates. Domestic scrap is sometimes costlier than imports due to unorganised-sector competition.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Exports reached eight countries and were about 37% of H1 FY27 revenue (Rs. 244 crore). Sales diversification is moving beyond Korea toward Thailand, Malaysia and China, mostly via trial orders following LME brand registration.

segments.name: Value-added lead alloys
segments.commentary: Value-added products are about 30% of volume and pure lead about 70%, per management. Alloy premiums vary with antimony content from 1% to more than 20%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 sales volume growth target of 10-15% maintained; management expects it to be achieved in H2 FY27, with Q3 and Q4 volume improvement seen.
Per-ton EBITDA expected to stay around current levels for now; management prioritises absolute EBITDA growth, expecting a better absolute level by year-end.
Capacity utilisation target of 70-75% on the expanded 1,56,950 MTPA installed capacity, up from 1,04,025 MTPA after debottlenecking (about 50% increase).
Management expects the debottlenecked capacity to contribute to volumes mainly next year (FY28), with the existing 10-15% growth partly from it.
Net foreign currency exposure stated at 5-10%, with exports acting as a natural hedge for imports.
Management expects EPR and RCM regulations to formalise scrap supply over 3-4 years, with the EPR seven-year window ending in about FY28-29.
risks_watch: Margin pressure: Q2 EBITDA margin of 8.9% and per-ton EBITDA of about Rs. 18,000 are down from prior levels; management expects no per-ton improvement near term, and procurement costs have not yet eased.
Raw material availability and cost: imported scrap cost rising with freight, insurance and shipping disruption (Hormuz); advance-to-supplier plan postponed.
H2 volume target of 10-15% growth for FY27 depends on procurement recovery; H1 growth was about 10%.
Debottlenecked capacity contributes only from next year, so utilisation stays below target for now.

Some figures were inconsistent in the call: Q2 FY27 EBITDA margin was stated as 8.9% in the CFO's remarks and 8.6% in a Q&A reference; prior-year Q2 volume was given as both 13,000 and 15,000 MT (15,000 MT was confirmed).

qa_highlights.question: Reyna Patel asked about key opportunities to expand the international customer base and how exports may contribute over the next 2-3 years.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said sourcing now spans 80-plus countries (vs 50-plus earlier) and sales are being extended from Korea to Thailand, Malaysia and China, mostly via trial orders after LME registration; no export contribution target was given.

qa_highlights.question: Yash Kabra asked why EBITDA and margins fell sharply, and the outlook for Q3, Q4 and next year.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY26 average EBITDA margin was about 12% and the year-on-year comparison against 19% was not ideal; cited higher RM freight, fuel and opex with a lag. Focus is absolute growth, with a better absolute level expected by year-end.

qa_highlights.question: Shubham Purohit asked whether the 10-15% volume growth target is intact and when debottlenecked capacity will contribute.
qa_highlights.answer: Target maintained and to be achieved in H2 FY27; debottlenecked capacity did not contribute in Q2 and is expected to contribute mainly next year, with FY27 growth partly from it.

qa_highlights.question: Shubham Purohit asked about the EBITDA per ton dip and the sustainable level for FY27-28.
qa_highlights.answer: Per-ton EBITDA fell to about Rs. 18,000 from about Rs. 19,000 (Q1) and Rs. 21,000 (prior year) due to imported RM costs, domestic sourcing premium and fuel/opex; guidance is to maintain current levels for now.

qa_highlights.question: Yash Kabra asked about lead price movements and outlook.
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no price outlook; LME lead was in the USD 1,850-1,950 range in Q1 and Q2 and is broadly at that range now; supply is the constraint as traders hold scrap when prices are low.

qa_highlights.question: Vivek Jhala asked whether working capital is the constraint on utilisation and about the net FX exposure.
qa_highlights.answer: Raw material availability, not working capital, is the main constraint; funds are available. Net FX exposure is 5-10%, with exports as a natural hedge.

qa_highlights.question: Pranav Jain asked about the rise in trade receivables and whether sourcing advances and job work are being used to recover volumes.
qa_highlights.answer: No big receivable discounting in the current fiscal year as IPO proceeds were used for working capital; PAT margin to decline. Advance-to-supplier plan postponed due to shipping and insurance costs; job work volumes were small in Q2 and are targeted to rise.

qa_highlights.question: Ravi Mehta asked for Q2 and H1 year-on-year volumes and whether per-ton margins will hold.
qa_highlights.answer: Q2 FY26 volume was about 15,000 MT vs 15,656 MT in Q2 FY27; H1 33,300 MT vs 30,700 MT; management agreed margins per ton should stay at current levels while volume grows.

capex_capacity: Installed capacity raised from 1,04,025 MTPA to 1,56,950 MTPA via debottlenecking, about 50% increase; management targets 70-75% utilisation.
Debottlenecked capacity did not contribute to Q2 FY27 volumes; management expects it to contribute mainly next year (FY28), with FY27's 10-15% growth partly from it.
Debottlenecking required less capex because existing machines were replaced/resized on a brownfield basis; management said this gave buffer capacity above the earlier neck-to-neck level.

Additional 6-acre land parcel at Naidupeta, Andhra Pradesh, next to existing facility; official handover to the company done, earlier only an allotment letter. Concrete expansion plans to be shared in a few months.

Evaluating adjacent copper and plastic recycling; lithium-ion recycling under evaluation but copper needs much larger capital and lithium-ion economics depend on rules, chemistry and raw material availability.
demand_pricing: Q2 FY27 volume 15,656 MT vs about 15,000 MT in Q2 FY26; H1 FY27 volume 33,300 MT vs 30,700 MT in H1 FY26 (about 10% growth). Q1 to Q2 volume described as broadly flat.
Management maintains FY27 volume growth target of 10-15% and expects to achieve it in H2 FY27; some volume improvement seen in October-November.

EBITDA per ton about Rs. 18,000 in Q2 vs about Rs. 19,000 in Q1 and about Rs. 21,000 in prior-year period (per analyst). Management guided per-ton margins to stay at current levels; priority is absolute EBITDA growth.

Procurement costs have not eased: imported scrap and freight/insurance rising due to war and Hormuz disruption; procurement cost increases lag into P&L by 2-3 months. Domestic scrap is sometimes costlier due to unorganised-sector competition.

Domestic battery scrap share of procurement about 27-28% vs about 15% a year earlier. Value-added lead alloys about 30% of volume, pure lead about 70%; alloy premium varies with antimony content from 1% to above 20%.

Exports to eight countries, about 37% of H1 FY27 revenue (Rs. 244 crore); diversifying from Korea to Thailand, Malaysia and China via trial orders after LME brand registration. Sourcing from 80-plus countries vs 50-plus earlier.

LME lead prices in the range of USD 1,850-1,950 per tonne; management gave no outlook. Supply constrained as scrap traders hold stock when LME is lower; demand from domestic and export markets described as good.
Net foreign currency exposure 5-10%; exports act as natural hedge against imports. Job work volumes were present in Q2 but very small versus past quarters.

summary.management_tone: Cautious on margins and near-term procurement, with management repeatedly saying raw material costs have not eased and per-ton margins will stay at current levels. Confident on volume recovery and capacity, though several answers were hedged on timelines (new land plans, Lithium-ion evaluation, copper) and some figures were inconsistent during the call.

adds.what: Debottlenecking raising installed capacity from 1,04,025 MTPA to 1,56,950 MTPA (about 50% increase), not yet contributing to Q2 FY27 volumes
Additional 6-acre land parcel at Naidupeta, Andhra Pradesh, handed over; concrete expansion plans to be shared in a few months

growth.why: FY27 volume growth target of 10-15% maintained (midpoint 12.5%), expected in H2 FY27 with H1 volume only ~10% up; debottlenecked 1,56,950 MTPA capacity (about 50% above 1,04,025 MTPA) targeted at 70-75% utilisation but expected to contribute mainly in FY28, so FY27 delivery is only partly backed by specific capacity and per-ton margins are guided flat.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 FY27 EBITDA margin fell to 8.9% (vs about 19% prior-year comparison per analyst) and per-ton EBITDA slid to about Rs. 18,000 from Rs. 19,000 in Q1 and Rs. 21,000 a year ago; management guides per-ton margins flat with imported scrap and freight costs not yet easing.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Debottlenecking already took installed capacity to 1,56,950 MTPA from 1,04,025 MTPA (about 50% up), but it did not contribute to Q2 FY27 and is expected to contribute mainly in FY28; new Naidupeta land is handed over with expansion plans due in a few months.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 10-15% volume growth target maintained and expected in H2; H1 FY27 volume was 33,300 MT, up about 10% from 30,700 MT, and October-November showed some improvement, though Q1 to Q2 was broadly flat.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Naidupeta 6-acre parcel is handed over and concrete expansion plans are to be shared in a few months, but no capex amount is given and utilisation is only targeted at 70-75% on the enlarged base, so a new capex call is not firm.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management held the 10-15% volume target and guided per-ton margins flat, with H1 volume only about 10% up and procurement costs still rising, so there is no sign of an upgrade.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: H2 volume target depends on procurement recovery and H1 growth was about 10% vs the 10-15% target, while imported RM and freight costs have a 2-3 month lag into the P&L and have not eased.

rows.label: Export diversification to Thailand, Malaysia and China
rows.why: Exports were about 37% of H1 FY27 revenue (Rs. 244 crore) across eight countries, and sales are moving beyond Korea via trial orders after LME brand registration, but no export contribution target was given.

rows.label: Borrowings reduction
rows.why: Borrowings were Rs. 35 crore at 30 Sep 2026 and management aims for gradual reduction, with raw material availability rather than working capital the main constraint.

rows.label: EPR and RCM formalising scrap supply
rows.why: Management expects EPR and RCM rules to formalise scrap supply over 3-4 years, with the seven-year EPR window ending around FY28-29, but the benefit is not quantified.
